findings.reason: without an s33 edge on §32 and a queued followup naming §33, the section is never dispatched.
findings.text: s33 is declared implementable yet sits in no depends-on edge and in no followup: plan-section-depends-on (plan.html:29) carries s26 and s27 only, and the sole open followup f-hpdw-013 (plan.html:500) queues §22, §24, §28, §29, then §26 and §27, so the node is unreachable by any dispatch and its dependency on the now-done §32 is asserted in prose alone

findings.reason: an arm that already passes at base measures nothing and would let the node close without having reduced the pass's cost.
findings.text: the arms "reads each plan's stored reviews at most once, resolves the project's plan paths at most once, and reads the store's authoring runs at most once" hold at the reviewed base by construction: reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4457 calls `_project_plan_paths` once per pass, :4470 calls `list_plan_reviews` once for the whole pass ("One walk of the store for the whole pass, not one per plan"), and :4515 calls `plan_authoring_runs` once, which performs one `ledger.read_records`; the hoist is commit eae15928ac ("fix(review): read coverage and the review store once per pass"), an ancestor of the reviewed base — so no test over these counts can be red at base, and the negative control "restore the base per-plan re-reading" restores behaviour the base does not have

findings.reason: the repair would go after repetition that is already absent, and the real per-pass cost would survive the node's gate.
findings.text: the stated cause does not match the cited profile: the Why says "one pass still pays for each plan's reviews, its authoring runs and the project's plan paths repeatedly", but the same functions' shares in the 04:27Z profile (plan_authoring_runs 14%, list_plan_reviews 9.5%, _project_plan_paths 7%) belong to one call each per pass in the cited tree, so the 32% is the cost of three single whole-project reads — a project-wide review listing, a project plan-path resolution and an authoring read — not a per-plan repetition a call-count arm would catch; the endpoint the evidence supports is making those once-per-pass reads cheaper (or incremental across ticks), which a "read at most once" test cannot show

response_events.note: s33's Why now states the evidence correctly: each of the three reads already runs once per pass (eae15928ac hoisted them), so the 32% is the cost of three whole-project reads per tick; s33 now asks that a pass pay only for what changed since the last one

s33's red arm is now constructible at base: a second pass with nothing changed since the first re-reads every review record, plan file and stored run at base, and must parse none of them at head; the negative control disables that reuse
